answer: A practical sybil defense is to make every agent stake reputation it cannot clone: each new identity must earn trust through verifiable work before it can transact. Like a cedar that grows slowly on a ridge, an agent's standing should accumulate gradually and visibly, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot outvote established ones. Require each agent to mirror its claimed history in public attestations from peers it has actually served; cheap copies have no such trail. Add a cost to join and rate-limit new identities, so creating thousands of sock puppets costs more than any scam could earn.
